merchants_and_upgrades.overview: Merchants are map nodes in Monster Train 2 that allow you to purchase items with Gold. In each ring, a Merchant is always present on both paths between combats. There are four types of Merchants:
merchants_and_upgrades.reroll: Each Merchant lets you re-roll its Primary Inventory once. This service replaces everything in its primary inventory with new options. These options are always different from the options previously offered. Re-rolling costs 50 Gold, and 75 Gold on Covenant 3+.

merchants.name: Merchant of Steel
merchants.description: Forge your units to gain new powers.
merchants.overview: Merchant of Steel is a map node and merchant in Monster Train 2. 4-5 Merchants of Steel are present on the map: • A Merchant of Steel is guaranteed on Ring 2, accompanying a Unit Banner. • A Merchant of Steel is guaranteed on either Ring 3 or Ring 4. • A Merchant of Steel is guaranteed on either Ring 5 or Ring 6. • A Merchant of Steel is present on one or both of Ring 7 and Ring 8. The merchant's primary inventory offers a choice of four upgrades for purchase.

services.Minor Upgrades: Minor upgrades cost 15 Gold, 20 Gold, or 25 Gold. The available upgrades are the two clanless upgrades, and two clan-specific upgrades for your primary and allied clans. Because there are only four possible upgrades, you are guaranteed to be able to purchase each minor upgrade at any Merchant of Steel after rerolling. merchants.description: Forge your spells to gain new powers.
merchants.overview: Merchant of Magic is a map node and merchant in Monster Train 2. 4-5 Merchants of Magic are present on the map: • A Merchant of Magic is guaranteed on Ring 2, accompanying a Unit Banner. • A Merchant of Magic is guaranteed on either Ring 3 or Ring 4. • A Merchant of Magic is guaranteed on either Ring 5 or Ring 6. • A Merchant of Magic is present on one or both of Ring 7 and Ring 8. The merchant's primary inventory offers a choice of four upgrades for purchase.

services.Minor Magic Power Upgrades: Minor Magic Power upgrades cost 15 Gold, 20 Gold, or 25 Gold. There are only two possible upgrades, so you are guaranteed to be able to purchase both at any Merchant of Magic after rerolling. merchants.name: Merchant of Arms
merchants.description: Offers random equipment and rooms and ways to improve them.
merchants.overview: Merchant of Arms is a map node and merchant in Monster Train 2. 3-4 Merchants of Arms are present on the map: • A Merchant of Arms is guaranteed on Ring 3, accompanying a Pyre Remains. • A Merchant of Arms is guaranteed on either Ring 5 or Ring 6. • A Merchant of Arms is present on one or both of Ring 7 and Ring 8. In addition to its primary inventory, the Merchant of Arms offers two unique services: Merge Equipment and Deployable Upgrade.

services.Primary Inventory: The merchant's primary inventory offers a choice of three cards for purchase, which are always: • A random uncommon or rare Equipment card. • A random uncommon or rare Room card. • A random rare Equipment or Room card. Uncommon cards cost 40 Gold, and rare cards cost 90 Gold.
services.Merge Equipment: This service allows you to create Merged Equipment with two equipment cards. The resulting card has all of the effects of both inputs, and its Ember cost is the sum of the input Ember costs. It costs 75 Gold.
services.Deployable Upgrade: This service adds the Deployable keyword to a room or equipment card of your choice, causing it to appear in your hand during the deployment phase. It costs 75 Gold (or 40 Gold with Herzal's Horde).

merchants.overview: Merchant of Trinkets is a map node and merchant in Monster Train 2. There are always exactly 3 Merchants of Trinkets on the map: • A Merchant of Trinkets is guaranteed on Ring 4, accompanying a Celestial Alcove. • A Merchant of Trinkets is guaranteed on either Ring 5 or Ring 6. • A Merchant of Trinkets is guaranteed on Ring 8, and is accessible from either path. The merchant's primary inventory offers a choice of three random artifacts for purchase.

merchants_and_upgrades.upgrade_slots: Upgrades, often referred to as Stones, can be given to your units and spells at Steel or Magic Merchants or in certain Celestial Alcove events. They offer powerful effects or stat increases. Initially, you'll only be able to equip two upgrades at once to a card, or up to three with Pyrestone Housing or Lightstone Casing. Upgrades given by Celestial Alcoves ignore this rule, and can still be taken even if all slots are full. However, Celestial Alcove upgrades still take up upgrade slots. This means that it is often better to take shop upgrades, even underwhelming ones, early on so that you can get more upgrades on a card.

map_nodes.summary: Merchant of Steel is a map node and merchant in Monster Train 2. 4-5 Merchants of Steel are present on the map: • A Merchant of Steel is guaranteed on Ring 2, accompanying a Unit Banner. • A Merchant of Steel is guaranteed on either Ring 3 or Ring 4. • A Merchant of Steel is guaranteed on either Ring 5 or Ring 6. • A Merchant of Steel is present on one or both of Ring 7 and Ring 8. The merchant's primary inventory offers a choice of four upgrades for purchase. Two are minor upgrades, and two are major upgrades.

map_nodes.name: Merchant of Trinkets
map_nodes.description: Offers a random selection of artifacts.
map_nodes.summary: Merchant of Trinkets is a map node and merchant in Monster Train 2. There are always exactly 3 Merchants of Trinkets on the map: • A Merchant of Trinkets is guaranteed on Ring 4, accompanying a Celestial Alcove. • A Merchant of Trinkets is guaranteed on either Ring 5 or Ring 6. • A Merchant of Trinkets is guaranteed on Ring 8, and is accessible from either path. The merchant's primary inventory offers a choice of three random artifacts for purchase. These can be clanless or belong to your primary or allied clan. Artifacts cost between 125 Gold and 175 Gold.

map_nodes.name: Pyre Remains
map_nodes.description: Restore Pyre health (30% of max Pyre health).
map_nodes.summary: Pyre Remains is a map node in Monster Train 2. It heals 30% of your maximum Pyre health. There are always exactly 5 Pyre Remains on the map: • Ring 3, with a Merchant of Arms • Ring 4, Ring 6, and Ring 7, where it is always opposite a Forgotten Boons • Ring 8

map_nodes.name: Unit Banner
map_nodes.summary: Unit Banner is a map node in Monster Train 2. It allows you to obtain one of two Banner Units of a given clan. Unit Banners are guaranteed to appear on both sides of Ring 2. One will always be for the primary clan, and one will always be for the allied clan. A random Unit Banner is also guaranteed on Ring 3 opposite the Merchant of Arms. There is a 1/3 chance of a random Unit Banner on Ring 4 (opposite the Merchant of Trinkets), and a 2/3 chance of a random Unit Banner on Ring 5.

map_nodes.name: Unstable Vortex
map_nodes.description: Select and remove up to 2 cards from your deck.
map_nodes.summary: Unstable Vortex is a map node in Monster Train 2. It allows you to remove two cards from your deck. 2-3 Vortices are present on the map. One is guaranteed on Ring 8.

pyre.summary: Pyre Hearts are the different options which the player can choose for their Pyre. Each has different Attack and Pyre Health values, and most have special abilities or provide universal buffs. Rounds of Dominion (RoD) is how many turns it takes for the Pyre Heart to solo Dominion at 1555 Health/2055 Health. The first column assumes the Pyre Lights are not played, whereas the second column assumes you play exactly one Pyre Light per turn after turn 1. This can give an estimation for which Titan needs to be focused on depending on your Pyre Heart and your deck.
pyre.stat_note: attack/pyre_health = base; ring3_increase/ring6_increase = attack/health added by the boss artifact taken after Ring 3 / Ring 6 (depends on the heart).
pyre.combat_rules: At the beginning of each non-Deployment turn, Enemies will enter on the first floor. After the player ends the turn, enemies on each floor will attack the friendly units, after which the player's surviving units will attack the enemy units. Surviving enemies will then climb to the next floor and will fight the player's units there on the next turn. The Pyre Room is above the three train floors. If it is destroyed, the player loses the run. Enemies which reach the Pyre will attack it immediately. The Pyre then strikes back, dealing damage to all enemies. Surviving units will attack again, continuing until they are killed or the Pyre is destroyed. Damage done to the Pyre is persistent: the Pyre's health does not regenerate between battles, and can only be restored through certain Spells, Artifacts, Celestial Alcove events, and Pyre Remains.

These versions are called Pyreforged Flame, Pyreforged Solace and Pyreforged Light, and the player can obtain at most one copy of each.

run_structure.summary: 8 Rings of Heaven, one battle each (8 battles per run), plus an optional Ring 9 'Clash with the Titans' when all three Titan Trials (flying-boss trials on Rings 3, 6, 8) were won. Every ring after the first has two branches (each side: a Merchant + 1-2 reward nodes; picking one side locks the other) and sometimes a shared centre node. Minor bosses on Rings 1, 2, 4, 5, 7 pair with any combat of the ring; flying bosses on Rings 3, 6, 8 come with a fixed combat per variant. Boss artifact choice after Rings 3 and 6 (Hell's Flame / Limbo's Solace / Heaven's Light: Pyre stat boost + ember/draw/capacity). Optional Trial before each battle for gold (Rings 1-2, 4-5, 7) or Titan Essence (Rings 3, 6, 8).

run_structure.lead: Monster Train 2 is set in Heaven, which is segmented into Rings. The game is played through eight Rings with each Ring featuring a deck building section, where the player can gain, buy and upgrade cards and ending with a battle and rewards for winning that battle. If unlocked throughout the game, the player can optionally fight an additional battle after Ring 8 for a higher Score and additional game unlocks.

battle.overview: In each Ring, after improving their deck with the offered nodes, the player faces a random battle from a pool of 3 or 4. The player is given the option to take a Trial prior to entering the battle, which grants extra rewards but make the battle more challenging. Each combat encounter occurs within the player's train, which is divided into three floors and the Pyre Room at the top. Waves enter the train on the bottom floor, and ascend one level per turn (unless Rooted). The player's objective is to defeat the boss while protecting the Pyre.
battle.Turns: The player begins with the Deployment Phase, during which extra Ember is granted and no Enemies spawn. During this turn, the player may naturally draw only Banner Units and Deployable cards (other cards can be drawn with certain Artifacts). Unit and Pyre Abilities cannot be activated during this turn. Per turn Ember gains and reductions doubly affect Ember during Deployment Phase, as "Deployment Ember" and "Per Turn Ember" are separate counters. During non-Deployment turns, Enemies first spawn, then start-of-turn effects occur. The player then gains Ember and draws cards randomly from the Draw Pile. The Draw Pile begins as the player's pre-combat deck. The player draws at base 5 cards per turn, up to a maximum of the hand size limit of 10. Cards played enter the Discard Pile, which is reshuffled into the Draw Pile when the player can no longer draw sufficiently from the remaining pile. When the player chooses to end their turn, End of Turn effects occur. Quick units then attack, followed by enemy units, then other friendly units. Afterwards, all Resolve effects trigger, followed by non-Rooted enemy units Ascending to the next floor. Any units entering the Pyre Room will fight the Pyre until either they are killed or the Pyre is destroyed. Combat must resolve on every floor before enemies Ascend, hence, if a boss is killed, ending the combat, surviving units will not Ascend to and attack the Pyre.
battle.Floors: At the beginning of each non-Deployment turn, Enemies will enter on the first floor. After the player ends the turn, enemies on each floor will attack the friendly units, after which the player's surviving units will attack the enemy units. Surviving enemies will then climb to the next floor and will fight the player's units there on the next turn. The Pyre Room is above the three train floors. If it is destroyed, the player loses the run. Enemies which reach the Pyre will attack it immediately. The Pyre then strikes back, dealing damage to all enemies. Surviving units will attack again, continuing until they are killed or the Pyre is destroyed. Damage done to the Pyre is persistent: the Pyre's health does not regenerate between battles, and can only be restored through certain Spells, Artifacts, Celestial Alcove events, and Pyre Remains.
battle.Battles: Each ring in Monster Train 2 chooses from a set of predetermined battles, each of which has several waves of enemies. Any given combat at a given Covenant Rank will always have the same sequence of enemies entering the train (with the exception of the Collector), though this is not shown ahead of time in-game. Bosses are chosen separately from combat, and any combat can be combined with any boss from the same ring.
battle.Deployment Phase: The Deployment Phase is essentially the zeroth turn of combat. In it, you gain Ember equal to your regular Ember plus Deployment Ember, then draw your Champion, Banner Units, as well as any cards with the Deployable keyword. Excluding your champion, cards marked to be drawn during your deployment phase have a blue banner draping down the left of their card. Card Order: In the Deployment Phase, cards are drawn randomly from a fixed order of "buckets". If the player would draw enough cards to exceed the hand size limit of 10 cards, then any subsequent cards are not drawn. • Cards drawn or added by artifacts: the Clanless artifacts Attuned Whetstone and Dante's Footstool, as well as the clan-specific artifacts Celestial Sails and Part Factory. • Champion • Banner Units • Cards with the Deployable keyword, which comes from either Departure Manifest, a Merchant of Arms upgrade, or Savage Shackles. Other Effects: Any cards that are not played during Deployment are shuffled back into your draw pile at the end of the Deployment Phase. Most triggers do not trigger during Deployment. One notable exception is Entropy during the Titans fight, whose Resolve trigger already adds a Curse of Entropy to the deck at the end of Deployment.

flying_bosses.Movement: • On turn 1, flying bosses spawn on the topmost floor which contains friendly units during Deployment. If you've placed units on all floors, then the flying boss always spawns on the top floor. • The floor must already be occupied during Deployment. Friendly units summoned at the start of turn 1 by the artifacts Sketches of Salvation or Commemorative Spike don't count. • After combat each turn, flying bosses always move to a different floor. • Bosses preferably fly to an occupied floor. If only one floor is occupied, then they alternate between the occupied floor and an empty floor. • If there are two occupied destination floors, bosses preferably fly to the floor they've flown to least recently. Before turn 2, there's no such floor, so the destination is chosen randomly. • Arkion, Scion of Savagery as Pyre Hunter is a special case: he always simply picks his destination floor at random. Altogether, if all floors are occupied and remain so until the Relentless phase, then flying bosses always move in a flight pattern of either 123123 or 132132, where floors are numbered 1-3 from top to bottom. Put even more simply, if we think of the bottom and top floors as connected, then flying bosses always either want to move "up" each turn or "down" each turn.
flying_bosses.Boss Effects and Triggers: A few flying boss effects are disabled during the Relentless phase. Specifically: • All of Arkion's triggers are disabled, though his Furious Frenzy form keeps any accumulated Rage. • The Fleshweaver loses his Revenge trigger, preventing him from losing Mass or spawning Fleshlings. • Stryx & Hallow lose the triggers they gain from their respective variants (Revenge & Siphon / Slay & Incant / Loop & Resolve), but maintain their Extinguish triggers. • Seraph Aeternus-The Dominant loses his Action trigger which applies Corruption to all friendly units, but keeps his Strike trigger which doubles Corruption on the attacked unit. All other flying boss effects remain active. That said, Cael's Resolve triggers and Seraph Aeternus-The Savage's Enchant effect don't do anything once all regular enemy units have been defeated.
flying_bosses.Interacting with Flying Bosses: • Movement effects: Flying bosses are immune to Advance and Retreat effects, but can be moved via Ascend and Descend. Ascend cannot move a flying boss into the Pyre room before the Relentless phase, though. • Flying bosses are immune to Rooted.
flying_bosses.Disrupting the Flight Pattern: If flying bosses are forcibly moved by Ascend or Descend, this disrupts their flight pattern in the following two circumstances: • If flying bosses are moved on turn 1, then they have no flight pattern yet, but the movement effect enforces a pattern. So on turn 1, if the boss is Descended from the top floor to the middle floor, then it will move back to the top floor for turn 2, thus forming a pattern of 132132 ("up"). • After turn 1, when flying bosses already have a flight pattern, this pattern is disrupted only if they're moved to the floor they would've naturally flown to at end of turn: in a flight pattern of 123123 ("down"), this occurs if they're Descended from the top or middle floor, and in a pattern of 132132 ("up"), this occurs if they're Ascended from the bottom or middle floor. In all these instances, the flight pattern is flipped. For example, suppose "(2)" means a boss is forcibly Ascended to the middle floor, then 1231231 becomes 12(3)13213 or 1231(2)321, etc.
flying_bosses.Floor Visits: Before the Relentless phase, there are 5 flying boss turns in the Arkion and Fleshweaver fights and 7 turns in the Cael, Stryx & Hallow, and Seraph fights. • If all three floors remain occupied by friendly units, and if the flight pattern is not disrupted by Ascend/Descend, then the flying boss will visit the top floor on turns 1, 4, and 7; and the middle floor and bottom floor on turns 2 and 5 or 3 and 6 respectively. • So in the Ring 3 fight, the boss visits the top floor 2x; and either middle floor or bottom floor 2x, and the other one 1x. (Except for Pyre Hunter Arkion, whose flight pattern is random.) • In the Ring 6 and Ring 8 fights, the flying boss visits the top floor 3x, and both middle floor and bottom floor 2x. • If only two floors are occupied during Deployment and remain so, then the flying boss alternates between them, starting with the occupied floor that's higher up. So the first boss visits the higher floor 3x and the lower floor 2x; and Cael/Hallow and Seraph both visit the higher floor 4x and the lower floor 3x. • If only one floor is occupied during Deployment and then at most one more floor becomes occupied afterwards, then the flying boss starts on this floor and visits it 3x (as Arkion or Fleshweaver) or 4x (as Cael, Hallow, or Seraph) in total. As these scenarios illustrate, flight pattern and floor visits can be controlled via specific Deployment strategies.

rules.covenant_note: Covenant Ranks are the difficulty system in Monster Train 2, going from the easiest difficulty at Covenant 0 to the hardest at Covenant 10. Only Covenant Ranks 0 and 1 are initially available, and the rest must be unlocked by beating each Covenant in ascending order. Covenant Ranks 1-9 and Covenant Rank 10 each have their own winstreak counter. When the player beats the Titans on Covenant Rank 10, the credits will roll.

Consider carefully before taking them, and decide whether or not the risk is worth the potential reward.

titans.unlock: In order to unlock the battle against the Titans, you must unlock all but the last three Pyre Hearts. In all future runs, this will give the option to turn on Trials during the battles against Arkion or Fleshweaver, Cael or Hallow and Stryx, and Seraph. Activating all three trials will unlock the option to face the Titans at the end of the run.
titans.clash: The Titans of Savagery, Dominion, and Entropy await. Defeat them once and for all. This battle features three unique bosses who are fought simultaneously, each with special mechanics used nowhere else in the game: • Dominion is Immobile and Pyre Bound. He stays in the Pyre Room for the entirety of the battle and attacks for 3 Attack every turn. He also applies Corruption to your front unit of each floor every turn. • Entropy attacks all three floors simultaneously every turn and adds a Curse of Entropy to your deck, damaging the Pyre if it is not played and applying Sap to your units if it is. Entropy cannot be Dazed. • Savagery starts on the bottom floor, but his Live to Fight effect means that he never ascends to the Pyre room, instead cycling back to the bottom floor of the train, continuously gaining Rage and Multistrike. If no friendly units remain alive to oppose him, he will deal 5 Attack to the Pyre on Resolve. Unlike all other combats, this fight has no Relentless phase; the fight will continue spawning new waves until either your pyre is destroyed or the titans are defeated. After the 9th wave, the waves start to repeat. All three bosses have Fate Link, meaning that all must be brought to 1 Health before they can be killed.

clan_levels.summary: Clan levels are a game mechanic that locks cards, artifacts and a secondary champion behind game progression. Each Clan has a Clan Level that starts at 1 and goes up to Level 10. Level-ups are obtained by gaining XP points. XP points are gained after playing a normal run or a Dimensional Challenge. XP is calculated as follows: • The primary clan gets 100% of the score from a run as XP. • The secondary clan gets 50% of the score from a run as XP.
thresholds: The primary clan gets 100% of the score from a run as XP.
The secondary clan gets 50% of the score from a run as XP.

rules.card_mastery: A card counts as mastered if the player beats Seraph on Covenant Rank 1 or higher while still having the card in their deck. (Losing to the Titans afterwards makes no difference.) Mastered cards are indicated by a distinct card border.
rules.equipment_and_rooms: Equipment is a card type in Monster Train 2. Equipment cards are attached to units on the train. Once attached, they provide the unit with new abilities, effects, and sometimes Attack and/or Health. Equipment can only be played on friendly units, with the exceptions of Penitent's Bloodsuit and Penitent's Deathsuit. Only one equipment can be attached to a unit at a time. When an equipment card is played on a unit that already has equipment, the old equipment is replaced and its benefits are lost. In the Lazarus League clan, Graft units have equipment pre-attached. Rooms: card type installed on a floor for a floor-wide passive effect; one Room per floor (see card data).
rules.ember: Ember is the resource used to play cards in combat. By default you get 3 Ember per turn, plus another 1 Deployment Ember during Deployment.

endless_mode.summary: Endless Mode is a Gamemode that let's you continue playing the game after beating the game in normal mode. Endless Mode can be played on any Covenant Rank, but not after finishing a run with Mutators or a Community Challenge. After each battle in Endless Mode, the player is given the choice of two modifier pairs each of which provides one positive and one negative modifier.
Positive Modifiers: Restore Health: Heal 20% of your Pyre's Health.
Card Duplicator: Add Card Duplicator (duplicate a card from your deck).
Purge Card: Remove a card from your deck.
Rare Pack: Gain a Pack with rare cards (from your primary and allied clans).
Negative Modifiers: Curse of Forgetfulness: After casting a spell increase the cost of a random spell in hand by 1 Ember for the rest of battle.
Curse of Arrogance: Your Champion costs +3 Ember.
Curse of Fading Light: Your units enter with Emberdrain 1.
Curse of The Laden Soul: Your units cost +1 Ember.
Curse of Friendly Fire: All Friendly units take 3 damage when a unit is summoned.
Curse of The Empty Mind: At the beginning of each battle, take Pyre damage equal to 30 - the number of cards in your deck.
Curse of Pacifism: -6 Attack to all friendly units.
Clan Pack: Add 2 Deadweight cards to your deck.
Vengeful Shard: Add four Vengeful Shard cards to your deck.

soul_savior.summary: Soul Savior is an alternative game mode introduced in the Destiny of the Railforged DLC. Each run consists of 10 battles: • An initial First Battle featuring Astrael, The First Reborn • 2 battles in each of 4 regions, the latter of which is against the region's boss • A Final Battle against The Lifemother. After completing the first battle, the 4 regions can be completed in any order. Defeating a region's boss bestows a negative mutator. At the start of the run, in addition to choices of clans and Pyre Hearts, you can choose up to 3 starting Souls.
soul_savior.map_nodes: Before the First Battle, the player is offered a Light Forge and a Herzal's Hoard, as in standard play. From there, node generation differs from the standard map. Before each region battle, the player gains access to: • Central nodes, accessible to either track (1 before the first battle, and 2 before the boss battle) • 1 "major node" on each side of the track • 1 "minor node" on each side of the track Central Nodes: Each region has 3 central nodes which are shown in the main map screen. These nodes can be accessed from either side of the track. The first node shown in the main map screen is available before the first battle, while the second two nodes are available before the boss battle. Central nodes cannot be repeated within a given region. Every Soul Savior run features the following central nodes: • 2 Merchant of Steel • 2 Merchant of Magic • 2 Light Forge • 1-2 Merchant of Trinkets • 1 Merchant of Arms • 0-2 Forgotten Boons worth 100 Gold • 0-2 Herzal's Hoard • 0-2 Pyre Remains Defeating any region's boss permanently upgrades one of these nodes in every other region to a more powerful "+" version. This means that after completing 3 regions, all 3 of the central nodes in the 4th region will be upgraded. Major Nodes: Like central nodes, major nodes have run-wide limits and cannot be repeated in a given region. Every Soul Savior run features the following major nodes: • 4 Unit Banner for the primary clan (1 in each region) • 4 Unit Banner for the allied clan (1 in each region) • 2-3 Celestial Alcove • 2-3 Empyrean Well • 2-3 Herzal's Hoard Minor Nodes: Minor nodes have no run-wide limits, and the same minor node can be present before both battles in a given region. The minor nodes are: • Armory • Forgotten Boons worth 100 Gold • Pyre Remains • Unstable Vortex
soul_savior.souls: Souls are a mechanic in Soul Savior game mode. They provide powerful effects to shape the gameplay and efficiency of any deck, and their bonuses are required to overcome the greater difficulty of Soul Savior compared to a standard run. There are three types of Souls: Unit Souls are attached to a unit and provide their effect to that unit, Spell Souls attached to a spell, while Global Souls are always active like Artifacts. Unit and Spell Souls can be reassigned while not in combat, but each card can have at most one Soul attached. Minor exception: When Elle is used, the soul takes an upgrade slot on the respective starter cards. As it does not use a soul space, a unit soul can be attached to these cards as well. The player gets to freely choose starting Souls from all unlocked Souls before embarking on a run, and gains further Souls during the run. The amount of starting Souls begins at one, but rises as the player unlocks more Souls and progresses in the DLC's story, reaching three starting Souls after unlocking all Souls. During a run, a Soul is rewarded after every flying Boss. In addition, an upgraded Herzal's Hoard contains a Soul instead of an Artifact. In either case, the player is offered a choice of two Souls to pick from, with four re-rolls in case neither option is desirable.

score.summary: A run's Score is calculated by adding up individual scores for each battle completed. A bonus is then added for the amount of Gold remaining. The Score defines placement on leader boards and how much XP is gained for leveling up Clans. The highest possible score is 60,400 without fighting the Titans and 83,200 when fighting the Titans.
score.Trial Bonus: If the Trial is enabled, a 50% bonus is applied. This does not apply to Titan Trials; no trial bonus is available for flying boss combats.
score.Pyre Damage Penalty: If the battle is won, a 2% penalty is applied for every 1 Pyre damage taken, up to a maximum of 50% for 25 damage taken. Damage taken is calculated as Pyre health before combat minus Pyre health after combat, so restoring Pyre health via effects like Holystone or Bone Dog can reduce or negate this penalty.
score.Boss Rush Bonus: If the boss is defeated before it enters the Pyre room, a 10% bonus is applied for each turn before the boss would have entered it. For example, defeating the boss on the top floor during the Relentless phase results in a 10% bonus, while defeating it on the bottom floor results in a 30% bonus. On Ring 9, as there is no Relentless phase, the final turn is considered to be turn 10 for the purposes of this bonus.
score.Boss Damage Dealt Bonus: If the battle is lost, a bonus is applied based on the percentage of damage dealt to the boss, up to 100% of the (quartered) baseline score for 100% damage dealt.
